title: Hom from an ideal-power torsion module is unchanged under flat neighbourhood base change
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a flat map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], let $I\subseteq R$ be a finitely generated ideal for which $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism, and let $K,N$ be $R$-modules with every element of $K$ annihilated by some power of $I$. Then scalar extension [def-weil-module-base-change] induces a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_S(K\otimes_RS,N\otimes_RS)$, $u\mapsto u\otimes_RS$. The bijection is natural in both modules.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EC (lemma-neighbourhood-equivalence, line 24301), part (2), case of torsion source

proof.text: First suppose that $N$ is $I$-power torsion. The canonical map $c_N:N\to N\otimes_RS$, $n\mapsto n\otimes1$, is bijective by [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-module-flat-base-change-iso]. It is $R$-linear and natural in $N$. The scalar-extension adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-extension-hom] gives $\operatorname{Hom}_S(K\otimes_RS,N\otimes_RS)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,N\otimes_RS)$, sending an $S$-map $v$ to $k\mapsto v(k\otimes1)$. Composition with $c_N$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,N\otimes_RS)$. Under these bijections, $u\in\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,N)$ goes to the unique $S$-map with value $c_N(u(k))=u(k)\otimes1$ on $k\otimes1$, namely $u\otimes_RS$. Thus the asserted Hom map is bijective when the target is torsion.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EC (lemma-neighbourhood-equivalence), proof of part (2), case N is I-power torsion; Algebra, Lemma 05DQ (lemma-adjoint-tensor-restrict)

proof.text: For arbitrary $N$ put $T=N[I^\infty]=\{n\in N:I^mn=0\text{ for some }m\ge1\}$, with inclusion $j:T\hookrightarrow N$. Since $I$ is finitely generated, [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-submodule-flat-base-change-iso] says that $T\to(N\otimes_RS)[(IS)^\infty]$, $n\mapsto j(n)\otimes1$, is bijective. The module $T$ is $I$-power torsion, so $c_T:T\to T\otimes_RS$ is bijective by [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-module-flat-base-change-iso]. The composite $(j\otimes_RS)\circ c_T$ equals the preceding map; therefore $j\otimes_RS:T\otimes_RS\to N\otimes_RS$ is injective and its image is exactly $(N\otimes_RS)[(IS)^\infty]$. Moreover $K\otimes_RS$ is $(IS)$-power torsion: by the same torsion-module comparison every element is $k\otimes1$ for some $k\in K$, annihilated by $I^m$ for some $m$, hence by $(IS)^m$ as an $S$-module.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EC (lemma-neighbourhood-equivalence), proof of part (2), reduction through part (1) to N[I^infinity]

proof.text: Every $R$-linear map $u:K\to N$ has image in $T$: if $I^mk=0$, then $I^mu(k)=0$. Thus composition with $j$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,T)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,N)$, with inverse by corestriction. Every $S$-linear map $v:K\otimes_RS\to N\otimes_RS$ likewise has image in $(N\otimes_RS)[(IS)^\infty]$ because its source is torsion by step 2. As $j\otimes_RS$ is injective with precisely this image (step 2), composition with it gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_S(K\otimes_RS,T\otimes_RS)\to\operatorname{Hom}_S(K\otimes_RS,N\otimes_RS)$. The square formed by these two bijections and the scalar-extension Hom maps commutes: $(j\circ u)\otimes_RS=(j\otimes_RS)\circ(u\otimes_RS)$ on pure tensors. The top Hom map is bijective by step 1 with the torsion target $T$; hence the bottom map in the statement is bijective. Every comparison and factorization is natural in $K$ and $N$, since the torsion-submodule assignment and scalar extension commute with module maps.
